request.system:
You are a football (soccer) coach's assistant. You answer one player's questions about
their own instep kicks, which a separate system measured from side-on video. You see the
measurements only through the tools.

Rules:
1. Call tools to get the data; never guess a value. If a question needs several pieces of
   data, call several tools.
2. Every number you write must be copied from a tool result (you may round an angle to
   whole degrees). Do no arithmetic: the tools give changes and comparisons ready-made.
3. If a feature was not measured, say so and give the tool's reason. Don't describe or
   judge it.
4. Knee values are interior angles between thigh and shin (180 = straight). Call them
   angles, never an amount of "bend" or "flexion"; a smaller number is a more bent knee.
5. The measurements can say what changed, not why. Report what changed, what else changed
   in the same sessions, and whether the change is bigger than the typical measurement
   error. Don't invent causes.
6. When you use a coaching passage, say it in your own words and put its ID in square
   brackets, e.g. [K-12]. Cite a study comparison by its norm_ref, e.g. [N-032]. Use only
   IDs the tools returned.
7. Questions that aren't about this player's kicks or how to improve them: say briefly
   that you can only help with their measured kicks. Call no tools for them.
8. Short, plain answers a teenager would understand. No medical advice.

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: The player's stored kick sessions, newest first: date, whether the clip was accepted (or why it was refused), each feature's value or why it wasn't measured, and the faults found. With feature_id, also that feature's trend over those sessions: values oldest first, the change from first to last, each step's change, and whether the change is larger than the measurement's typical error.

feature_id.description: The feature whose trend to compute.

tools.name: get_session_features
tools.description: Everything measured in one session: each feature's value, unit and definition, or why it wasn't measured; the faults found with their thresholds and where each threshold comes from; or why the clip was refused.

tools.name: compare_to_norms
tools.description: Compares one feature of one session with published study values (verified norm rows): the verdict, the study's mean, SD and band, its population and caveats; and the fault rule on that feature, if any, with its threshold and source.

tools.name: search_drills
tools.description: Searches short coaching passages (cues, drills, explanations) quoted from published coaching sources. Returns the best 3 with their IDs and sources. Give fault_id when the question is about one of these faults: the search is then limited to passages about it, which works better.

query.description: What to look for, in words.

parts.text: Has my knee extension speed improved?

refused_because: camera not side-on: shoulder width is 0.67 of torso length in the kick (> 0.5, heuristic). Film from the side, level with the hips
sessions.note: the clip was refused by the quality check, so nothing was measured

trend.definition: fastest knee straightening speed before contact

typical_error.why: this feature's accuracy hasn't been measured
